title: Finite direct sums of finite-presentation modules are finite presentation
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space and $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; being abelian, it is additive, so any two objects have a biproduct [def-weil-additive-category]. Let $\mathcal G,\mathcal H$ be $\mathcal O_X$-modules of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] (every $x\in X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ such that the restriction to $U$ is isomorphic to the cokernel, in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, of an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ with $m,n\in\mathbf N$). Then the biproduct $\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal H$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is of finite presentation.

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PJ (label lemma-directed-colimit-diagram-finite-presentation), proof, first paragraph after the claim: 'Since a direct sum of finitely presented O_X-modules is finitely presented' (asserted without proof); the notion is Modules, Definition 01BN (label definition-finite-presentation, modules.tex)

proof.text: Notation and coproduct property of $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$. For an open $U\subseteq X$, $\mathcal O_U$, $\mathcal F|_U$ (sections $\mathcal F(W)$, $W\subseteq U$ open) and the free module $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ with basis sections $e_1,\dots,e_n$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]; on morphisms $(\alpha|_U)_W=\alpha_W$, so restriction is a functor sending zero maps to zero maps. Let $\varepsilon_i:\mathcal O_U=\mathcal O_U^{\oplus1}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ be the map $e_1\mapsto e_i$. By the definition node, for every $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal M$ the $\mathcal O_U$-linear maps $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal M$ are exactly the maps $e_i\mapsto s_i$ for arbitrary $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal M(U)$ (with $s_i=f(e_i)$ recovered from the map $f$), and in the case $n=1$ the maps $\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M$ are exactly $e_1\mapsto s$, $s\in\mathcal M(U)$. Hence a family $f_i:\mathcal O_U\to\mathcal M$ ($f_i(e_1)=s_i$) has exactly one $f:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal M$ with $f\varepsilon_i=f_i$ for all $i$, namely $e_i\mapsto s_i$: $(\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n},(\varepsilon_i)_i)$ is a coproduct of $n$ copies of $\mathcal O_U$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, i.e. a colimit of the discrete diagram of $n$ copies [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Modules, Definition 01BN (label definition-finite-presentation) and the description of maps out of O_U^{\oplus n} by sections recorded in the definition node

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$. By the definition of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation] applied to $\mathcal G$ there are an open $U_1\ni x$, integers $m_1,n_1$, an $\mathcal O_{U_1}$-linear map $a_1:\mathcal O_{U_1}^{\oplus m_1}\to\mathcal O_{U_1}^{\oplus n_1}$ and an isomorphism $\mathcal G|_{U_1}\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_1)$; applied to $\mathcal H$ it gives $U_2\ni x$, $m_2,n_2$, $a_2:\mathcal O_{U_2}^{\oplus m_2}\to\mathcal O_{U_2}^{\oplus n_2}$ and $\mathcal H|_{U_2}\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_2)$. Put $U=U_1\cap U_2$, an open neighbourhood of $x$ contained in both.

Restriction of the presentation of $\mathcal G$ from $U_1$ to $U$ (Step 1). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-colimit-restriction] to the ringed space $(U_1,\mathcal O_{U_1})$ and the open $j:U\hookrightarrow U_1$. For $W\subseteq U$ open, the inverse image $j^{-1}\mathcal M$ there has sections $\mathcal M(W)$: the presheaf inverse image is $\varinjlim_{V\supseteq W}\mathcal M(V)$ over opens $V$ of $U_1$ containing $W$, and $V=W$ is the smallest of them, so the colimit is $\mathcal M(W)$ and this presheaf is already a sheaf. Hence $j^{-1}$ is the restriction $(-)|_U$ of Step 0, $(\mathcal G|_{U_1})|_U=\mathcal G|_U$ and $\mathcal O_{U_1}|_U=\mathcal O_U$. (i) $\mathcal O_{U_1}^{\oplus n_1}$ with the maps $\varepsilon_i$ is a coproduct of $n_1$ copies of $\mathcal O_{U_1}$ (Step 0 on $U_1$), i.e. a colimit of a discrete diagram [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]; by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-colimit-restriction] its restriction with the restricted coprojections is a coproduct of $n_1$ copies of $\mathcal O_U$, hence there is an isomorphism $
u:\mathcal O_{U_1}^{\oplus n_1}|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n_1}$ compatible with the coprojections (two coproducts of one family are isomorphic by the unique map compatible with the coprojections); likewise $\mu:\mathcal O_{U_1}^{\oplus m_1}|_U\cong\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m_1}$. (ii) The cokernel $c_1:\mathcal O_{U_1}^{\oplus n_1}	o\operatorname{Coker}(a_1)$ is a colimit of the diagram formed by the parallel pair $a_1,0$; by the same lemma $c_1|_U$ is a colimit of the pair $a_1|_U,0|_U=0$, i.e. a cokernel of $a_1|_U$. (iii) Applying the functor $(-)|_U$ to the isomorphism $\mathcal G|_{U_1}\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_1)$ gives $\mathcal G|_U\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_1)|_U\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_1|_U)$. (iv) Put $a_1'=
u\circ a_1|_U\circ\mu^{-1}:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m_1}	o\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n_1}$; then $c_1|_U\circ
u^{-1}$ is a cokernel of $a_1'$ (a map $f$ out of $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n_1}$ kills $a_1'$ iff $f
u$ kills $a_1|_U$, as $\mu$ is invertible), so $\mathcal G|_U\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_1')$. The same argument with $U_2$ gives $a_2':\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m_2}	o\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n_2}$ and $\mathcal H|_U\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_2')$.

proof.text: $(\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal H)|_U\cong\mathcal G|_U\oplus\mathcal H|_U$. In an additive category [def-weil-additive-category] a biproduct $A\oplus B$ with $i_A,i_B,p_A,p_B$ is a coproduct of $A,B$ with coprojections $i_A,i_B$: for $f:A\to T$, $g:B\to T$ the map $h=fp_A+gp_B$ satisfies $hi_A=f$, $hi_B=g$ (from $p_Ai_A=\mathrm{id}$, $p_Bi_A=0$ and symmetrically), and any $h'$ with $h'i_A=f$, $h'i_B=g$ equals $h'(i_Ap_A+i_Bp_B)=fp_A+gp_B$. So $(\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal H,i_{\mathcal G},i_{\mathcal H})$ is a coproduct, i.e. a colimit of the discrete diagram $\{\mathcal G,\mathcal H\}$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], in $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-space-colimit-restriction] (for $U\subseteq X$, with $j^{-1}$ identified with $(-)|_U$ as in Step 2) $((\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal H)|_U,i_{\mathcal G}|_U,i_{\mathcal H}|_U)$ is a coproduct of $\mathcal G|_U,\mathcal H|_U$ in $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$. The biproduct $\mathcal G|_U\oplus\mathcal H|_U$ in the abelian, hence additive, category $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ is another coproduct of the same pair, so the unique map between them compatible with the coprojections is an isomorphism.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01AH (label lemma-limits-colimits) (2): colimits in Mod(O_X); restriction to an open as in Sheaves, Section 009E

proof.text: Biproducts of cokernels. Let $\mathcal A$ be an additive category [def-weil-additive-category], and for $k=1,2$ let $a_k:Q_k\to P_k$ be a morphism with cokernel $c_k:P_k\to C_k$ (so $c_ka_k=0$ and every $f:P_k\to T$ with $fa_k=0$ is $gc_k$ for a unique $g:C_k\to T$; in particular $c_k$ is an epimorphism). Put $a=i_{P_1}a_1p_{Q_1}+i_{P_2}a_2p_{Q_2}:Q_1\oplus Q_2\to P_1\oplus P_2$ and $c=i_{C_1}c_1p_{P_1}+i_{C_2}c_2p_{P_2}:P_1\oplus P_2\to C_1\oplus C_2$. By the biproduct identities $a\,i_{Q_k}=i_{P_k}a_k$, $c\,i_{P_k}=i_{C_k}c_k$ and $p_{P_l}i_{P_k}=\delta_{kl}$. Claim: $c$ is a cokernel of $a$. (i) $ca=i_{C_1}c_1a_1p_{Q_1}+i_{C_2}c_2a_2p_{Q_2}=0$. (ii) Let $f:P_1\oplus P_2\to T$ with $fa=0$. Then $(fi_{P_k})a_k=f\,a\,i_{Q_k}=0$, so $fi_{P_k}=g_kc_k$ for a unique $g_k:C_k\to T$. Put $g=g_1p_{C_1}+g_2p_{C_2}$; then $gc=g_1c_1p_{P_1}+g_2c_2p_{P_2}=fi_{P_1}p_{P_1}+fi_{P_2}p_{P_2}=f$. (iii) If also $g'c=f$, then $g'i_{C_k}c_k=g'c\,i_{P_k}=fi_{P_k}=g_kc_k$, so $g'i_{C_k}=g_k$ as $c_k$ is an epimorphism, and $g'=g'(i_{C_1}p_{C_1}+i_{C_2}p_{C_2})=g$. Hence $C_1\oplus C_2$ with $c$ is a cokernel of $a$, so $\operatorname{Coker}(a)\cong C_1\oplus C_2$.

proof.text: Rank bookkeeping. In $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$, $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m_1}\oplus\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m_2}$ with the $m_1+m_2$ composites $i_1\circ\varepsilon_j$, $i_2\circ\varepsilon_j$ is a coproduct of $m_1+m_2$ copies of $\mathcal O_U$: a family of maps out of the copies is first assembled on each $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m_k}$ (a coproduct by Step 0) and then on the biproduct of the two (a coproduct by Step 3), each time uniquely. Hence there is an isomorphism $\sigma:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m_1}\oplus\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m_2}\cong\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(m_1+m_2)}$, and likewise $\tau:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n_1}\oplus\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n_2}\cong\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(n_1+n_2)}$. For $a'=a_1'\oplus a_2'$ as in Step 4, put $b=\tau a'\sigma^{-1}:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(m_1+m_2)}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(n_1+n_2)}$, an $\mathcal O_U$-linear map; as in Step 2 (iv), composing with isomorphisms on both sides does not change the cokernel up to isomorphism: $\operatorname{Coker}(b)\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a')$.

source.place: Agent-written argument for the claim used in Properties, Lemma 01PJ proof; the categories are additive by Modules, Lemma 01AG (label lemma-abelian)

proof.text:
Conclusion. In the abelian, hence additive, category $\Mod(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], Step 3, Step 2 (with the biproduct of the two isomorphisms $\mathcal G|_U\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_1')$, $\mathcal H|_U\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_2')$, which is an isomorphism with inverse the biproduct of the inverses), Step 4 (applied to $a_1',a_2'$; cokernels are unique up to isomorphism) and Step 5 give
$$(\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal H)|_U\cong\mathcal G|_U\oplus\mathcal H|_U\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_1')\oplus\operatorname{Coker}(a_2')\cong\operatorname{Coker}(a_1'\oplus a_2')\cong\operatorname{Coker}(b).$$
So $x$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ on which $\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal H$ is the cokernel of a map $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(m_1+m_2)}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus(n_1+n_2)}$. As $x\in X$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal G\oplus\mathcal H$ is of finite presentation.
